title: Green Pastures
body: A shepherd doesn't force sheep to lie down in green pastures — he leads them somewhere safe enough to finally stop moving. Rest isn't something you force on yourself either. It's something you receive when you trust the One leading you.
application: Where in your week could you let God lead you to rest instead of forcing productivity?

title: New Every Morning
body: Whatever went wrong yesterday, God's mercy doesn't carry a grudge into today. His compassion resets each morning, not because you earned a clean slate, but because that is simply who He is.
application: Is there something from yesterday you're still carrying that God has already released?

title: The Narrow Place
body: "Out of my distress I called on the LORD; the LORD answered me and set me free." Distress is real in this verse — it isn't skipped over. But it isn't the final word either.
application: Name one distress you're in right now, honestly, in prayer.

title: Ordinary Obedience
body: "One who is faithful in a very little is also faithful in much." Most of the Christian life happens in unremarkable moments — a kind word, a kept promise, a quiet act of patience. God is not waiting for your big moment; He's present in your small ones.
application: What is one small, unnoticed act of faithfulness you can offer today?

title: Held, Not Hurried
body: "He will carry the lambs in his bosom." A shepherd carrying a lamb doesn't rush. God's pace for your growth is not the internet's pace, or even your own impatience. He carries you at a pace that actually forms you.
application: Where are you rushing something God might be forming slowly and well?
